_note: Hand-written. Only what each engine documents publicly, with source and date; behaviour (redirects, pings) is shown as observed, never with a stated purpose. Purposes and statements are paraphrased, not quoted, and presented as the company's own description, which Lens cannot check. Review every release.

cookies.NID: preferences such as language; Google also lists it for ads in its services to signed-out users and for personalised autocomplete in Search (about 6 months)
cookies.AEC: detecting spam, fraud and abuse in advertising (about 6 months)
cookies.UULE: precise location sent so results match where you are (up to 6 hours)
cookies.pm_sess: keeping the browser session and checking requests come from you (30 minutes)

server.signed_out: Google says that when you are not signed in it stores what it collects with identifiers tied to your browser or device, and that search and ad results may be customised with search activity even when you are signed out; it points to private browsing to avoid that.
server.signed_in: Google says that with Web & App Activity on, your searches and activity in its services are saved to your account, with details such as language, device, general location and IP address.

steps.label: Activity controls
steps.what: Turn Web & App Activity off, or off and delete what was saved.

steps.label: My Activity
steps.what: See and delete saved searches, and set automatic deletion.

steps.label: Google Takeout
steps.what: Download a copy of what is in your Google Account.

steps.label: Data protection request
steps.what: In the EU, EEA and UK: contact Google's data protection office, for example to ask for a copy of your data.

cookies.MUID: identifies unique browsers visiting Microsoft sites
cookies.MC1: identifies unique browsers visiting Microsoft sites
cookies.MSFPC: identifies unique browsers visiting Microsoft sites
cookies.TOptOut: records that you opted out of personalised advertising
cookies.NAP: encrypted demographic data based on your account profile

server.signed_out: Microsoft says that search history kept without an account can be cleared in Bing's settings, and that cookies such as MUID identify unique browsers visiting Microsoft sites.
server.signed_in: Microsoft says that when you are signed in, your searches are linked to your Microsoft account.

steps.label: Bing search history
steps.what: See and clear the search history Bing keeps, also without an account.

steps.label: Microsoft privacy dashboard
steps.what: Signed in: see and clear search and chat history linked to your account.

steps.label: Privacy requests
steps.what: Contact Microsoft's privacy team or Data Protection Officer, for example to ask for a copy of your data.

server.signed_out: DuckDuckGo says it does not save or share your search history and builds no profiles, and that its default cookies only store your settings.

steps.label: DuckDuckGo privacy policy
steps.what: Its own description, with how to use your privacy rights for the little it may hold.
